issues.legal_issue: The phrase covering any other public purpose is not limited to a purpose of the State, and includes a category distinct from State and Union purposes.
material_facts: The State requisitioned premises for a public purpose under a law that authorized requisition for a State purpose or any other public purpose.
The challenged requisition was considered in an appeal concerning whether the State had authority to make it.
issues.conclusion: The phrase “any other public purpose” denotes a category distinct from a State purpose and a Union purpose; the State may legislate for a public purpose that is not a purpose of the Union.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31 requires acquisition or requisition of property to be for a public purpose and with compensation. The Court read together entries 33 of List I, 36 of List II, and 42 of List III, which distinguish Union purposes, State purposes, and other public purposes. It rejected an ejusdem generis construction that would restrict “any other public purpose” to a State purpose, noting that such a reading would make those words surplusage. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.state_requisition_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a requisition made by a State government.
predicates.authorization_covers_state_or_other_publ: The governing authorization refers to a State purpose and also to any other public purpose.
predicates.requisition_serves_public_purpose: The requisition serves a purpose that benefits the public or a section of the public.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a State requisition made under an authorization covering State or other public purposes, and the requisition serves the public, the category of other public purposes is distinct from State purposes.

issues.legal_issue: Premises may be requisitioned to house a member of a foreign consular staff when the purpose is a State purpose or another public purpose, even if it also has a Union-purpose aspect.
material_facts: The premises were requisitioned to house a member of a foreign consulate’s staff.
The Court considered that the State had an interest in its trade and commerce and in the efficient discharge of the foreign consul’s duties within the State.
There was no duty on the Union to provide accommodation for the consular staff.
The appeal concerned the validity of the State’s requisition.
issues.conclusion: The requisition was valid: the purpose was more a State purpose than a Union purpose and, in any event, a Union-purpose aspect did not prevent it from also being a State or general public purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 6(4)(a) of the Bombay Land Requisition Act, 1948, premises could be requisitioned for a State or other public purpose. Article 31 applies to both Union and State legislation. Entries 33 of List I, 36 of List II, and 42 of List III identify the relevant legislative fields; entry 36 gives the State competence over requisition except for Union purposes. Although entry 11 of List I and Article 73 concern consular representation and Union executive power, securing accommodation for a consular staff member does not itself amount to providing consular representation, particularly where the Union has no duty to provide that accommodation. An undertaking or activity may serve State, Union, and general public purposes at the same time. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: state_requisition_challenge_appeal and requisition_for_foreign_consular_staff_housing and (serves_state_commercial_interest or serves_general_public_welfare or purpose_has_multiple_public_facets)

predicates.state_requisition_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a requisition made by a State government.
predicates.requisition_for_foreign_consular_staff_h: The State requisitions premises to house a member of a foreign consulate’s staff.
predicates.serves_state_commercial_interest: The accommodation helps the State protect or promote its own trade and commerce or supports the consul’s work within the State.
predicates.serves_general_public_welfare: The requisition serves a general public-welfare purpose.
predicates.purpose_has_multiple_public_facets: The purpose can serve State, Union, or general public interests at the same time.

issues.definition: A requisition challenged on appeal is valid when it provides housing for foreign consular staff and serves a State commercial interest, general public welfare, or purposes with multiple public facets.
